items.corrections: The named general EE roadmaps did not open, and the bounded primary-source search did not yield a readable current high-Tc materials result; no scalable ambient-pressure grid conductor was established.
A primary paper demonstrates 60 W at about 40% efficiency over two metres using resonant coils, far below the proposed tens-of-metres, kilowatt, >90% specification.
A Nature paper reports a parity-measurement component for a hybrid device, while explicitly stating the measurement alone does not distinguish topological Majorana modes from trivial Andreev states.
Experiments have shown visible-light cloaking for selected objects and polarization; the all-spectrum, lossless, zero-distortion cloak is not established.

Experimental and theoretical steep-slope device concepts show limited progress below the conventional room-temperature slope, but do not meet the claimed <5 mV/decade scalable high-current reliable transistor.
A 3072-electrode neural recording prototype was demonstrated in freely moving rats, but the system used a cable and neither millions of neurons nor bidirectional stimulation was demonstrated.

The review documents very low ambient RF power densities, insufficient direct device power and range/efficiency trade-offs, supporting the harvesting challenge without validating the universal efficiency target.

Electronic-photonic integration has reached a single-chip microprocessor with memory and light-based I/O, but its processing logic/memory remain electronic; this is not a photonic general-purpose processor.

Research papers and NREL material describe self-organizing/decentralized energy-grid concepts and distributed-control demonstrations, while not establishing universal stability or outage-free operation.

A review explicitly identifies path-loss and atmospheric-absorption barriers to combined Tbps/kilometre transmission. Its summaries of separate experiments do not provide an inspected primary demonstration of the exact practical transceiver.
